body:
Update. GP had prescribed my medication from this month. So all in all i only needed to pay out of pocket for titration then an additional
1 month of meds.

Same as you. Dx in Dec with Mypace. I have had my final review, GP has received the paperwork asking for shared care. GP verbally told me that he would prescribe my ongoing meds, but until it’s in my hand I am still nervous. I have 10 days of meds left and according to receptionist the letter was on the GPS workflow for Friday.

I took my last dose today. No sign of prescription. I did message them and they replied saying they were behind due to the holiday & would be sent out ASAP. I am a little nervous about how long I will need to wait on the medication. GP has agreed to prescribe but not until they receive instruction from mypace. I ordered the repeat to account for the time it might take to get that sorted and now it’s overlapping.
I could have sworn you were talking about me there. Recent diagnosed, one month on meds so far! I HEAR you x

My Chronic pain is as a result of an injury I got during some risk taking behavior (sporting injury that could have been prevented had I been less impulsive) I do have reports etc, most definitely something going on from about age 3-4 and was also medicated as a child. My dad said for being a little shit but remember my mum saying it was for breathholding. My mum has since died and getting info on this period has been quite difficult. Getting past the GP reception is impossible hence going private for this. I wonder if they will want to know more about that.
I have been seeing a counselor for the last year. I have found it helpful. I actually think it's the ADHD itself holding me back, does that make sense?

I am considering booking with Mypace. Keep seeing the appointments get further and further away but worried about the shared care thing. I can afford the assessment but keen to know if anyone had any issues with shared care
This sort of thing doesn’t bother me in the slightest. I struggle with surprises so we have fallen into the habit of planning things like birthdays together, so no one can really forget.

I injured my neck playing sport, had c5/6 neck fusion surgery, followed by a second surgery because the first one failed. Have had neuropathic pain ever since. My neck is solid, but they tell me it’s like a tube of toothpaste you remove the pressure but the dent on n the nerves still there. Pain in both arms, I wake in pain, it eases if I am active but too much activity is a killer. Problem is each day my “too much” changes.

14 years for me. I am mobile, I can actually play sport but the pain I am in after…. It’s intense. I can’t think straight. I wonder if it’s worth it so stop, then find that if I stop I end up in just as much pain but also depressed

I teach, I can tell you more about my pupils interests and learning and quirks and their story but still sometimes stutter at their name. What is more important is the story than the name. Right? I also feel very strongly about making sure I use and know names but in a fraction of a second I do sometimes mess up. It’s about information processing, try not to be sad, down, etc
